blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (The Authorization header is written to the logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store only a hash of the token (SHA-256 of the 32 random bytes is enough for a high-entropy secret; no bcrypt needed) in a `token_hash` column, hash the presented token in the middleware and look it up with `WHERE token_hash = $1` — still a simple indexed equality, so the stated reason for storing it as given does not hold. Anyone who reads the table (a SQL injection elsewhere, a leaked backup, a replica, a support dump) otherwise gets bearer credentials for every account, usable at once and, since revocation is deferred, impossible to cancel (CWE-312, CWE-256). Update task 1.1 and 1.2 accordingly.
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Redact credential headers before logging: drop or mask `Authorization` and `Cookie` (the middleware already authenticates by the `session=` cookie, so every browser session would leak too). Anyone with access to the logs — support, the log pipeline, a log aggregator — can copy a token or session and call the API as that user, with no way to revoke it in this change (CWE-532). To identify which token an integration sent, log a non-secret token id or a short prefix of its hash instead. Task 1.3's test `logs_requests` should assert the header is absent from the log.
findings.title: The Authorization header is written to the logs
